name: Forgewright
materials: Blackened hand-forged iron straps, square rivets and fleur finials around dark green smoked glass; a hair-thin champagne gold inlay runs inside every strap.
good: Strongest blacksmith identity; joints read as real load-bearing hardware; text areas stay calm; very clear HUD-to-Journal bridge.
watch: Fleur finials at every corner add up quickly; would need a lighter corner for small slots. Heaviest frame of the set.

name: Riverstone
materials: Honed dark slate with faint veining, bevelled stone mouldings, a bronze channel inlay and chevron keystone corners; panels sit on stone corbels.
good: Quiet, grounded and timeless; the most legible over the bright day scene; stone corbel joints are an original scaffolding idea.
watch: Stone can feel static and dungeon-like; slate veining must stay faint behind long text.

name: Bannercloth
materials: Dense green felted wool bordered by couched gold-thread vine embroidery; panels hang from slim iron rods with ball finials; heraldic roundel corners.
good: Most directly tied to the concept art's embroidered cloaks and banners; hanging-rod scaffolding is distinctive and literal; warm and lived-in.
watch: Embroidered borders are busy at small size; the heraldic eagle reads as a specific house and should become an Open Legend motif.

name: Reliquary
materials: Deep green champlevé enamel in gilt beaded frames with garnet and agate cabochons at the corners; hinge-straps join panels.
good: Most precious and refined; crisp at small sizes; beaded dividers and hinge joints are elegant.
watch: Reads royal or ecclesiastical rather than survival; heavy gold contradicts the current no-gold-border panel trial. Better reserved for rewards or rare items.

name: Lanternhorn
materials: Translucent green-tinted horn panes in wrought iron lantern cames with pierced quatrefoil vents; the lantern frame continues from panel to panel.
good: Ties directly to the lantern-light preference; pierced iron edges are beautiful; chain-hung joints feel physical.
watch: Mottled horn panes are too busy behind text in the kit; the assembled HUD toned them down. Pane texture must be calmed before use.

name: Cartographer
materials: Smooth deep green surface with a faint grid, champagne double rules with scale ticks, compass-rose corner roundels and engraved cartouche title rails.
good: Lightest and most modern; fits the hand-drawn map idea and a character who records the world; closest to the current Gildmoss restraint.
watch: Compass roses at every corner become repetitive; least tactile and least medieval-survival of the set.

name: Fieldworks
materials: Waxed green oilcloth stretched in dark ash-pole frames with forged iron clamps and plates; a tall pole carries the HUD and Journal like a camp signpost.
good: The most literal scaffolding: panels physically hang off one post; strongly survival-camp; plain plates read cleanly.
watch: Visible timber grain edges toward the rejected wood look; bent-pole connector is physically implausible; the post occupies screen edge.

name: Gambeson
materials: Dark green diamond-quilted linen, riveted mail bands with champagne edges, lamellar steel corner plates, leather straps and blackened buckles as joints.
good: Armour craft maps naturally to a combat-capable survival game; buckled straps are an original connector; quilting stays low behind text.
watch: Mail bands are visually noisy at small size; buckles must not suggest something you can click.

name: Antlerwork
materials: Ivory bone and antler strips with notch carving and iron pins around smooth dark green; antler-tine corners, bone toggles in iron rings.
good: Very original hunter-crafter identity; ivory edges give high contrast without gold; strongly about a wilderness world.
watch: Antler tines read slightly aggressive or tribal; ivory is bright and may compete with text on dark.

name: Gildmoss Crest
materials: Translucent green glass with top lantern light, a single champagne hairline rim and small engraved roundels only where panels join.
good: Closest to the chosen Gildmoss direction and the glass/lantern preferences; least frame weight, so the most world stays visible; compact size reads cleanly.
watch: Least 'medieval survival' character of the set; the faint star motif in roundels and buttons is generic and could take an Open Legend mark instead.

name: Brooch & Band
materials: Green felted wool edged with tablet-woven geometric bands; bronze penannular brooches pin neighbouring panels together.
good: Woven bands tie to the clothing in the concept art; the brooch pinning two panels is the most charming connector in the set; bands give pattern without metal weight.
watch: Kit corners drift toward interlace knotwork, close to the rejected knotted styling; bands are busy at compact size. The first kit sheet (kept as r0) had a title-substitution bug from my script, regenerated.

name: Verdigris
materials: Burnished green-black metal faces in hammered copper repoussé reed-and-wave bands with soft verdigris in the recesses; pinned copper clasps join panels.
good: Reed-and-river repoussé is the most specific to the riverside setting; patina gives a second green that suits the palette; joints are solid and physical.
watch: Raw copper reads brown-orange, close to the rejected brown palettes; frames are heavy and wide at compact size.
